stem: What is the key distinction between primary and secondary microcephaly?

options.text: Primary occurs in males, while secondary occurs in females
Primary is present at birth, while secondary develops postnatally after a normal birth measurement
Primary is caused by genetics, while secondary is caused by trauma
Primary involves the whole body, while secondary only involves the head
Primary is due to infection, while secondary is due to prematurity

explanation: Primary microcephaly is present at birth, whereas secondary microcephaly develops after birth following a previously normal head measurement.
rationale: The defining feature is timing: primary is evident at birth, while secondary appears later when head growth falls behind after an initially normal measurement.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because microcephaly classification is based on timing and head growth pattern, not sex.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because primary microcephaly is present at birth, while secondary microcephaly develops after birth following a normal initial measurement.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because either type may have genetic or acquired causes; the main distinction is when the small head size becomes evident.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because microcephaly refers specifically to head circumference, not overall body size.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because infection or prematurity may contribute to microcephaly, but they do not define the primary versus secondary distinction.

source.hint: Focus on whether the head was small when the baby was born or if it fell off the growth curve later.
